problem: Prior VLN agents mostly compress the navigation history into a fixed-size recurrent state (LSTM, or the recurrent state token in RecBERT). This condensed memory loses early observations on long trajectories. Earlier VLN transformers either ignore history (PREVALENT pretrains on instruction plus single-step observation only) or cannot predict actions (VLN-BERT scores instruction–path compatibility). None of them optimizes the visual representation for navigation end-to-end.
motivation: History matters for instruction grounding and environment understanding. Examples are 'bring the spoon to me', which requires remembering the start, and 'with the windows on your left', where the window is absent from the agent's oriented view. Keeping every past panorama is too expensive with a flat transformer, which costs O(t^2 K^2). Keeping only the oriented view (as in E.T.) discards critical information. Separately, large transformers are unstable to train with RL from scratch, and single-step pretraining without history overfits seen houses.
key_idea: Explicitly encode the full history of past panoramas and actions with a hierarchical ViT, which encodes views, then the spatial relations within each panorama, then the temporal relations across steps. Fuse this history with the instruction and the current panorama in a dual-stream cross-modal transformer. Train it end-to-end with VLN-specific proxy tasks (SAP/SAR, SPREL, MLM, MRM, ITM) before RL+IL fine-tuning.
insight:
Keeping the whole panoramic history as tokens, rather than a recurrent state, helps most on long-horizon tasks.
- From scratch with ResNet-152 on R2R val-unseen, hierarchical history beats recurrent (SR 54.4 vs 52.2, SPL 48.7 vs 47.0) and temporal-only (53.2/48.0).
- On R2R-Back val-unseen (proxy-task initialized), SR is 41.1 recurrent vs 45.1 temporal-only vs 56.5 hierarchical.
- History is also what makes proxy-task pretraining generalize. A PREVALENT-style no-history model with the same proxy tasks reaches only SPL 52.7 vs 57.5 for HAMT on val-unseen, because its SAP accuracy collapses on unseen houses; the authors attribute this to memorizing seen-house layouts.
- Proxy-task pretraining gives the largest single gain (val-unseen SR 54.4→63.5, SPL 48.7→57.5) and makes RL usable: RL alone reaches 63.5 SR vs IL alone 57.2, and RL+IL reaches 65.7/60.9.
- ViT features beat ResNet-152 (64.4/58.8), and end-to-end ViT tuning adds +2.1 SPL (60.9). End-to-end tuning only works with the two-stage schedule: single-stage gives SPL 53.5 vs 56.5 without e2e.
method: Unimodal encoders: a 9-layer BERT-style text transformer. Each observation view embedding is LN(W·ViT feature) + LN(W·[sinθ,cosθ,sinφ,cosφ]) + navigable/non-navigable/stop embedding + type embedding, with an appended STOP token.

Hierarchical history encoding: each past panorama (K=36 views) goes through ViT-B/16, then a 2-layer panoramic transformer for spatial relations. The views are average-pooled and residually added to the oriented-view feature, then summed with the action-angle, step and type embeddings plus a [cls] token. The resulting temporal sequence costs O(tK^2 + t^2) instead of O(t^2K^2) for a flattened history.

Cross-modal transformer: a 4-layer dual-stream (LXMERT-like) module. Text attends to vision (history concatenated with observation) and vice versa, followed by intra-modal self-attention. An encoder-decoder variant (noT2V) drops text-to-vision attention so text is encoded once, which is more efficient for long instructions (R4R, RxR, CVDN).

Proxy tasks (sampled per batch with MLM:MRM:ITM:SAP:SAR:SPREL = 5:2:2:1:1:1):
  - MLM, MRM (KL to ViT ImageNet class probabilities) and ITM (NCE with 4 negatives: 2 from other pairs, 2 temporally shuffled).
  - New SAP: classify the expert next view via f_SAP(o'_i ⊙ x'_cls).
  - New SAR: regress heading and elevation from x'_cls.
  - New SPREL: regress the relative heading/elevation between two views, with visual or angle features dropped at p=0.3.

Two-stage end-to-end training: 200k iterations with ImageNet ViT frozen (4 P100 GPUs), then 20k iterations fully end-to-end (20 V100 GPUs; learning rate 5e-5 for ViT and 1e-5 for the rest; RandAugment and stochastic depth).

RL+IL fine-tuning: A3C, with the critic applied to x'_cls ⊙ h'_cls. The reward combines distance reduction with an alignment/fidelity term, and stop gives ±2. The IL (SAP) loss has weight λ=0.2 and γ=0.9, training runs 100k iterations with unimodal encoders frozen, and inference uses greedy decoding. Task-specific rewards: distance-only for R2R-Last, REVERIE and CVDN; two-stop midpoint scheme for R2R-Back.

New benchmarks: R2R-Back (append a return command and require reaching the goal then returning to the start; SPL uses the full GT path length) and R2R-Last (only the last sentence of each R2R instruction).

setting.backbone: HAMT: ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-pretrained, fine-tuned end-to-end) + 9-layer BERT-style text transformer + 2-layer panoramic transformer + 4-layer dual-stream cross-modal transformer (trained). RxR variant: CLIP visual features (frozen) + multilingual BERT-initialized text encoder.
setting.model_size: not reported (ViT-B/16 image encoder + 9/2/4-layer transformers, roughly BERT-base scale)
setting.training_data: R2R train + PREVALENT's speaker-augmented instruction–trajectory pairs for proxy-task training. R2R fine-tuning uses the same augmented data as RecBERT. The other datasets (R4R, R2R-Back, R2R-Last, CVDN, REVERIE) are fine-tuned on their own train splits without augmentation. RxR uses RxR train for proxy tasks and fine-tuning.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views) with relative heading/elevation angle features; full history of past panoramas and action angles
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select a navigable candidate view or STOP)
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard nav-graph connectivity; REVERIE object features are extracted from ground-truth object bounding boxes (standard REVERIE setup)

numbers_note: State-of-the-art tables report the best of 2 runs, selected on val unseen. Ablation tables report mean±std over 2 runs, so ablation and SOTA numbers differ slightly: the full model's ablation val-unseen score is 65.7±0.7 SR / 60.9±0.7 SPL vs 66/61 in the SOTA table. R4R reports val unseen only. R2R-Back has no test split. The nDTW-vs-instruction-length analysis on R4R is in a figure only. The RxR results use CLIP features without end-to-end tuning, unlike the other benchmarks. REVERIE SPL values are printed as 30.20 / 26.67 in the table.
results: HAMT sets a new state of the art on seven VLN datasets. On R2R val-unseen it reaches SR 66 / SPL 61 vs RecBERT 63/57, and on test-unseen 65/60 vs 63/57. On R4R val-unseen: CLS 57.7, nDTW 50.3 vs RecBERT 51.4/45.1. On CVDN test the goal progress is 5.58 vs 3.91 for MT-RCM+EnvAg. On RxR test: SR 53.12 / nDTW 59.94 vs CLEAR-CLIP 40.29/53.69. On REVERIE, navigation SPL is 30.20 val-unseen / 26.67 test vs RecBERT 24.90/23.99. Gains are largest on long-horizon R2R-Back: val-unseen SR 57.2 vs RecBERT 41.1 and EnvDrop 32.4.
limitations: Restricted to discrete nav-graph navigation with panoramic candidate selection; continuous environments (VLN-CE) are left to future work. End-to-end ViT training is costly (20 V100 GPUs), and inference is about 1.5x slower than RecBERT (104 s vs 69 s on R2R val-unseen).

On REVERIE test, object grounding is worse than SIA (RGS 14.88 vs 19.02) and RecBERT (RGSPL 13.08 vs 13.51), because object features come from a ViT optimized on R2R rather than a detection-pretrained model.

Failure cases stem from scene and object recognition errors (e.g., missing a 'liquor shelf', unusual scenes). Single-stage end-to-end training underperforms, so the method depends on a careful two-stage schedule and on augmented data.
